added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(\Omega\subset\mathbb R^p\) be a bounded domain with piecewise \(C^1\) boundary, and let \(\vartheta\) have a density \(\lambda\in C^1(\overline\Omega)\) such that \(\lambda>0\) on \(\Omega\), \(\lambda=0\) on \(\partial\Omega\), and
\[
 I_{\mathrm{pr}}
 =\mathbb E_\lambda\!\left[
 \{\nabla\log\lambda(\vartheta)\}
 \{\nabla\log\lambda(\vartheta)\}^{\!\top}
 \right]
\]
is finite. Let \(P_\vartheta\) be dominated by a measure \(\xi\), with density \(p_\vartheta\), and suppose that \(p_\vartheta(x)\) is differentiable in \(\vartheta\) for \(\xi\)-almost every \(x\). The likelihood score is understood \(P_\vartheta\)-almost surely on \(\{x:p_\vartheta(x)>0\}\). Assume that differentiation may be passed under the integral sign, coordinate by coordinate, so that
\[
 \int \nabla p_\vartheta(x)\,d\xi(x)
 =\nabla\int p_\vartheta(x)\,d\xi(x)=0,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_\vartheta\{\nabla\log p_\vartheta(X)\}=0,
\]
and assume that the likelihood score is square integrable. Let \(\psi\in C^1(\overline\Omega)\), and let \(T=T(X)\) have finite joint squared risk. Finally, assume that coordinatewise integration by parts is valid for \((T(x)-\psi(\vartheta))p_\vartheta(x)\lambda(\vartheta)\), with zero boundary flux; explicitly, for each coordinate \(k\),
\[
 \int_{\partial\Omega}\!\int
 \{T(x)-\psi(\vartheta)\}p_\vartheta(x)\lambda(\vartheta)
 n_k(\vartheta)\,d\xi(x)\,dS(\vartheta)=0,
\]
and all integrals used in this integration-by-parts identity are finite. Define
\[
 I(\vartheta)=\mathbb E_\vartheta\!\left[
 \{\nabla\log p_\vartheta(X)\}
 \{\nabla\log p_\vartheta(X)\}^{\!\top}
 \right],\qquad
 M=I_{\mathrm{pr}}+\mathbb E_\lambda I(\vartheta),\qquad
 a=\mathbb E_\lambda\nabla\psi(\vartheta).
\]
If \(M\) is positive definite, then
\[
 \mathbb E\{T-\psi(\vartheta)\}^{2}\ge a^\top M^{-1}a.
\]
If \(M\) is singular, the score and integration-by-parts identity gives
\[
 a=\mathbb E\!\left[
 \{T-\psi(\vartheta)\}
 \{\nabla\log p_\vartheta(X)+\nabla\log\lambda(\vartheta)\}
 \right],
\]
which, under the stated finite-second-moment conditions, entails the necessary range condition \(a\in\operatorname{Range}(M)\); in that case the correct formulation is
\[
 \mathbb E\{T-\psi(\vartheta)\}^{2}\ge a^\top M^{+}a,
\]
where \(M^{+}\) is the Moore--Penrose inverse. If \(a\notin\operatorname{Range}(M)\), the displayed score identity and finite risk are incompatible, so the Moore--Penrose expression must not be used as an unconditional replacement for the ordinary inverse. The scalar formula is the case \(p=1\).

attestation.note: The displayed scalar-functional specialization is taken from Gill and Levit, Applications of the van Trees Inequality, Theorem 1; the stable DOI is supplied instead of a long verbatim transcription.

proposed_statement_changes.reason: The original citation omitted the score identity, differentiation-under-the-integral, and boundary integration-by-parts hypotheses used by van Trees, and it wrote an ordinary inverse without requiring positive definiteness. The replacement preserves the applied inequality while stating the singular case with its necessary range condition.

statement_notes.justification: This cited inequality is the classical Bayesian information lower bound used by Theorems 4 and 5. Its tightened statement makes the score identity, differentiation under the integral sign, zero boundary flux, positive-definite inverse case, and singular range condition explicit.
